subject: accountancy
book: Accountancy Part I (Partnership Accounts); Accountancy Part II (Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements) (NCERT, rationalised)

chapters.title: Part I: Accounting for Partnership: Basic Concepts

concepts.text: Definition of partnership under Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (Sec 4)
Essential features: two or more persons, agreement, business, sharing of profits, mutual agency, unlimited liability
Maximum number of partners (50 under Companies Rules 2014) and minimum two
Meaning of partnership deed and its usual contents (capital, profit ratio, interest, salary, drawings, admission/retirement terms)
Provisions applicable in absence of deed: equal profit sharing, no interest on capital, no salary/commission
Interest on drawings not charged and 6% p.a. interest on partner's loan in absence of deed
Interest on partner's loan as a charge against profit (not appropriation)
Items peculiar to partnership: capital accounts, appropriation of profit, reconstitution adjustments

sections.name: 1.4 Maintenance of Capital Accounts of Partners

concepts.text: Fixed capital method: separate capital and current accounts; items recorded in current account
Fluctuating capital method: single capital account recording all adjustments
Distinction between fixed and fluctuating capital accounts
Numericals: prepare partners' capital and current accounts under both methods
Profit and loss appropriation account: meaning, format and entries
Interest on capital: calculation on opening capital, adjustment for additions/withdrawals during year
Interest on capital when provided only out of profits: insufficient profit allocated in ratio of interest
Partner's salary and commission (commission on profit before or after charging it)
Transfer to reserve and sharing of remaining profit in profit-sharing ratio
Interest on drawings: fixed amount withdrawn on specific dates (product method)
Interest on drawings: equal amounts at beginning, middle or end of each month (6.5, 6, 5.5 months)
Interest on drawings: equal amounts at beginning/middle/end of each quarter (7.5, 6, 4.5 months)
Interest on drawings when date not given (six months average) and when rate is per annum vs flat
Calculating opening capital from closing capital (working back)
Numericals: prepare P&L appropriation account with all adjustments

sections.name: 1.6 Guarantee of Profit to a Partner

concepts.text: Meaning of guaranteed minimum profit to a partner
Deficiency borne by all other partners in their ratio
Deficiency borne by a particular partner
Deficiency borne by remaining partners in an agreed ratio; guarantee given by firm vs by a partner
Numericals: appropriation account with guarantee of profit
Need for past adjustments when interest/salary omitted or wrongly given after closing accounts
Preparing adjustment table (statement showing net effect) and single adjusting entry
Past adjustments when profits distributed in a wrong ratio
Numericals: adjustment journal entry for omissions of interest on capital, drawings, salary

chapters.title: Part I: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm: Admission of a Partner

sections.name: 2.1 Modes of Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm

concepts.text: Reconstitution: change in agreement due to change in profit-sharing ratio, admission, retirement or death, amalgamation
Adjustments required on admission: new ratio, sacrificing ratio, goodwill, revaluation, reserves, capitals
Rights acquired by new partner: share of assets and share of future profits
Capital and goodwill brought in by new partner
Calculating new ratio when new partner's share is taken from old partners in their old ratio
New ratio when sacrifice is in an agreed ratio or by a particular partner
New ratio when old partners surrender a fraction of their own share
Sacrificing ratio = old share - new share; use in goodwill distribution
Numericals: compute sacrificing and new profit-sharing ratios in various cases
Meaning and nature of goodwill as an intangible asset
Factors affecting value of goodwill: location, efficiency of management, market situation, nature of business, special advantages
Need for valuation of goodwill (change in PSR, admission, retirement, death, dissolution, amalgamation)
Average profit method: goodwill = average profit x number of years' purchase
Weighted average profit method
Normalising past profits for abnormal items before averaging
Super profit method: (average profit - normal profit) x years' purchase; normal profit = capital employed x normal rate
Capitalisation of average profits: capitalised value - actual capital employed
Capitalisation of super profits method
Numericals: compute goodwill under each method
AS 26: goodwill not recorded unless purchased; no goodwill account raised on admission
Premium for goodwill brought in cash: credited to sacrificing partners in sacrificing ratio
Premium retained in business vs withdrawn by old partners
Goodwill brought in kind (other assets) or premium partly brought
New partner unable to bring goodwill: debited to new partner's capital/current account
Existing goodwill in books written off among old partners in old ratio
Hidden goodwill: inferred from capital contributed and profit share
Numericals: journal entries for treatment of goodwill on admission

sections.name: 2.7 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

concepts.text: Reserves, P&L balance and workmen compensation reserve distributed among old partners in old ratio
Accumulated losses and deferred revenue expenditure (e.g. advertisement suspense) written off in old ratio
Investment fluctuation reserve and treatment of excess claim/decline in market value
Alternative: adjusting through a single entry without disturbing reserves

sections.name: 2.8 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

concepts.text: Revaluation account: increase in assets/decrease in liabilities credited; decrease in assets/increase in liabilities debited
Recording unrecorded assets and liabilities
Profit or loss on revaluation shared by old partners in old ratio
Preparing revaluation account, partners' capital accounts and new balance sheet (numerical)
New partner's capital calculated on basis of old partners' adjusted capitals
Old partners' capitals adjusted in new ratio on basis of new partner's capital; excess/deficiency settled in cash or current account
Calculating total capital of the firm from new partner's capital and share

sections.name: 2.10 Change in Profit Sharing Ratio among the Existing Partners

concepts.text: Sacrifice and gain on change in ratio; gaining partner compensates sacrificing partner for goodwill
Treatment of reserves, accumulated profits and revaluation on change in ratio
Numericals: journal entries and capital accounts on change in profit-sharing ratio

chapters.title: Part I: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm: Retirement/Death of a Partner

sections.name: 3.1 Ascertaining the Amount Due to Retiring/Deceased Partner

concepts.text: Items making up amount due: capital, current account, share of goodwill, reserves, revaluation profit, profit till date
Deductions: drawings, interest on drawings, share of losses
New ratio of remaining partners when retiring share is taken in old ratio or agreed ratio
Calculating new ratio when continuing partners acquire retiring share in specified proportions
Gaining ratio = new share - old share; difference from sacrificing ratio
Numericals: compute gaining and new ratios
Retiring/deceased partner's share of goodwill credited, continuing partners debited in gaining ratio (AS 26)
Writing off existing goodwill in old ratio
Hidden goodwill on retirement when amount paid exceeds dues
Numericals: journal entries for goodwill on retirement/death

sections.name: 3.5 Adjustment for Revaluation of Assets and Liabilities

concepts.text: Revaluation account on retirement/death; profit or loss shared by all partners in old ratio
Recording unrecorded assets and liabilities

sections.name: 3.6 Adjustment of Accumulated Profits and Losses

concepts.text: Distribution of reserves, P&L balance and other accumulated items in old ratio

sections.name: 3.7 Disposal of Amount Due to Retiring Partner

concepts.text: Payment in lump sum in cash
Transfer to retiring partner's loan account
Payment in instalments with interest; preparing retiring partner's loan account
Numericals: prepare capital accounts, loan account and balance sheet after retirement
Adjusting continuing partners' capitals in new ratio; total capital may be fixed
Bringing in or withdrawing cash to adjust capitals
Accounting on death similar to retirement; amount payable to executors
Share of profit till date of death on time basis (based on previous year/average profits)
Share of profit till date of death on turnover (sales) basis
Profit and loss suspense account for deceased partner's share
Deceased partner's capital account and executor's account
Numericals: prepare deceased partner's capital account and executor's account

chapters.title: Part I: Dissolution of Partnership Firm

concepts.text: Meaning of dissolution of partnership (reconstitution) vs dissolution of firm (business closed)
Distinction between dissolution of partnership and dissolution of firm
Dissolution by agreement
Compulsory dissolution (insolvency of partners, business becomes illegal)
Dissolution on happening of certain contingencies (expiry of term, completion of venture, death, insolvency)
Dissolution by notice in partnership at will
Dissolution by court (insanity, permanent incapacity, misconduct, persistent breach, losses, transfer of interest)
Section 48 order of payment: losses including capital deficiency; external liabilities; partners' loans; partners' capitals; surplus in profit ratio
Treatment of private assets and liabilities of partners
Realisation account: meaning and format
Transfer of assets (except cash/bank and fictitious) at book value to realisation account
Transfer of external liabilities to realisation account
Sale of assets and payment of liabilities through realisation account
Asset taken over by a partner; liability taken over by a partner
Creditors accepting an asset in full/partial settlement
Realisation expenses paid by firm vs paid/borne by a partner (with remuneration)
Unrecorded assets and liabilities realised or settled
Tangible assets taken at book value and intangibles at nil when realisable value not given
Profit or loss on realisation shared in profit-sharing ratio
Distribution of accumulated profits, reserves and losses among partners
Settlement of partner's loan account
Closing partners' capital accounts and cash/bank account
Numericals: prepare realisation account, partners' capital accounts and cash/bank account
Journal entries for dissolution transactions
Excluded: piecemeal distribution, sale to a company and insolvency of partners

chapters.title: Part II: Accounting for Share Capital

concepts.text: Company as artificial person with separate legal entity, perpetual succession, limited liability, common seal, transferability of shares
Separation of ownership and management
On basis of liability: companies limited by shares, limited by guarantee, unlimited companies
On basis of membership: private company, public company, one person company
Government companies, holding and subsidiary companies, associate companies
Meaning of share and nature of shares as movable property
Preference shares: preferential rights to dividend and capital repayment
Types of preference shares: cumulative/non-cumulative, participating/non-participating, convertible/non-convertible, redeemable/irredeemable
Equity shares: residual rights, voting, fluctuating dividend
Categories: authorised (registered/nominal) capital
Issued and unissued capital
Subscribed capital: subscribed and fully paid up; subscribed but not fully paid up
Called-up and uncalled capital; paid-up capital; reserve capital
Presentation of share capital in balance sheet (under shareholders' funds) and in notes to accounts
Numericals: show share capital in balance sheet and notes to accounts
Process: prospectus, application, allotment, calls; minimum subscription 90%
Issue for cash: lump sum vs instalments (application, allotment, first and final calls)
Journal entries for share application, allotment and calls (with and without separate call accounts)
Issue at par
Issue at premium; uses of securities premium (Sec 52)
Issue at discount not permitted except sweat equity (Sec 53)
Calls in arrears and calls in advance; calls in arrears/advance accounts (interest excluded)
Under-subscription
Over-subscription: rejection and refund of excess applications
Pro-rata allotment and adjustment of excess application money to allotment and calls
Numericals: journal entries and cash book for share issue with over-subscription and pro-rata allotment
Issue of shares for consideration other than cash (purchase of assets/business; number of shares calculation)
Issue of shares to promoters/vendors
Private placement of shares
Employee stock option plan (ESOP)
Sweat equity shares
Meaning and reasons for forfeiture of shares for non-payment of calls
Forfeiture of shares issued at par: entries and share forfeiture account
Forfeiture of shares issued at premium when premium is received vs not received
Forfeiture of shares allotted on pro-rata basis (calculating amount unpaid)
Presentation of share forfeiture account in balance sheet
Re-issue at par, premium or discount (discount limited to forfeited amount)
Transfer of balance of forfeited shares account to capital reserve on re-issue
Re-issue of only part of forfeited shares; proportional capital reserve calculation
Numericals: journal entries for forfeiture and re-issue, with balance sheet presentation

chapters.title: Part II: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

concepts.text: Debenture as acknowledgement of debt with fixed interest; debenture trust deed
Bonds and debentures as borrowed (debt) capital
Differences: ownership vs creditorship, return (dividend vs interest), voting rights, security, repayment priority, conversion
On basis of security: secured and unsecured (naked) debentures
On basis of tenure: redeemable and perpetual (irredeemable) debentures
On basis of convertibility: fully convertible, partly convertible and non-convertible debentures
On basis of coupon rate: specific coupon rate and zero coupon rate debentures
On basis of registration: registered and bearer debentures
Issue for cash: lump sum and in instalments (application and allotment)
Over-subscription of debentures and refund/adjustment
Issue at par, at premium and at discount (journal entries)
Securities premium on debentures and its use
Journal entries for over-subscribed debenture issue

sections.name: 6.6 Issue of Debentures for Consideration other than Cash

concepts.text: Debentures issued to vendors for assets/business purchased; number of debentures calculation
Goodwill or capital reserve when purchase consideration differs from net assets

sections.name: 6.7 Issue of Debentures as a Collateral Security

concepts.text: Meaning of collateral security
First method: no journal entry, shown in note to accounts under the loan
Second method: debentures account credited and debenture suspense account debited
Balance sheet presentation of collateral debentures
Six cases: issue at par/premium/discount combined with redemption at par or premium
Loss on issue of debentures account and premium on redemption of debentures (liability)
Numericals: journal entries for issue with terms of redemption
Note: actual redemption of debentures (methods, DRR, sinking fund) is not in the CBSE syllabus
Calculation of interest at coupon rate on face value; half-yearly payments
Journal entries for interest due, payment and transfer to statement of profit and loss (TDS excluded)

sections.name: 6.10 Writing off Discount/Loss on Issue of Debentures

concepts.text: Discount/loss written off in year of allotment
First from securities premium (if any), balance to statement of profit and loss as finance cost
Numericals: write off discount/loss on issue of debentures

chapters.title: Part II: Financial Statements of a Company

concepts.text: Financial statements as end products of accounting: balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, notes, cash flow statement
Based on recorded facts, accounting conventions, postulates and personal judgements
Information about economic resources and obligations, earning capacity, cash flows, management performance
Companies Act 2013 Section 129 and Schedule III format
Balance sheet format: Equity and Liabilities and Assets with major headings
Shareholders' funds: share capital, reserves and surplus, money received against share warrants
Share application money pending allotment
Non-current liabilities: long-term borrowings, deferred tax liabilities (net), other long-term liabilities, long-term provisions
Current liabilities: short-term borrowings, trade payables, other current liabilities, short-term provisions
Non-current assets: property, plant and equipment and intangible assets (tangible, intangible, capital work-in-progress, intangible assets under development)
Non-current investments, deferred tax assets (net), long-term loans and advances, other non-current assets
Current assets: current investments, inventories, trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents, short-term loans and advances, other current assets
Operating cycle and criteria for classifying items as current or non-current
Notes to accounts: purpose and contents
Statement of profit and loss format: revenue from operations, other income, total income
Expenses: cost of materials consumed, purchases of stock-in-trade, changes in inventories, employee benefits, finance costs, depreciation and amortisation, other expenses
Profit before tax, tax expense and profit for the period
Exercise type: classify given items under major heads and sub-heads of Schedule III
Excluded: exceptional items, extraordinary items and discontinued operations

sections.name: 7.5 Uses and Importance of Financial Statements

concepts.text: Report on stewardship, basis for fiscal policy, credit decisions, investment decisions, labour contracts, information to public
Not exact (estimates), historical in nature, ignore price-level changes, ignore qualitative aspects, may be window-dressed, biased

chapters.title: Part II: Analysis of Financial Statements

sections.name: 8.1 Meaning of Analysis of Financial Statements

concepts.text: Analysis as studying relationships among financial statement items to judge profitability and financial position
Analysis vs interpretation

sections.name: 8.2 Significance of Analysis of Financial Statements

concepts.text: Usefulness to finance manager, top management, trade payables, lenders, investors, labour unions and others

sections.name: 8.3 Objectives of Analysis of Financial Statements

concepts.text: Assessing earning capacity, managerial efficiency, short-term and long-term solvency, inter-firm and intra-firm comparison, forecasting

sections.name: 8.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements

concepts.text: Comparative statements, common-size statements, ratio analysis, cash flow analysis
Horizontal (across periods) vs vertical (within one period) analysis
Comparative balance sheet: absolute change and percentage change between two years
Comparative statement of profit and loss
Interpretation of comparative statements
Numericals: prepare comparative balance sheet and statement of profit and loss
Common-size balance sheet: each item as % of total assets/total equity and liabilities
Common-size statement of profit and loss: each item as % of revenue from operations
Numericals: prepare common-size statements and interpret
Ignores price-level changes, qualitative aspects, historical, window dressing, affected by accounting policies and personal bias
Ratio as an arithmetical relationship between two related figures; forms: pure ratio, percentage, times, fraction
Knowing operational efficiency, liquidity, solvency, profitability; inter-firm and intra-firm comparison
Helps understand efficiency of decisions, simplifies complex figures, helps comparative analysis, identifies problem areas, SWOT, planning and forecasting
Limitations of accounting data, ignores price-level changes, qualitative factors, window dressing, varied accounting policies, no standard ratios
Traditional classification: statement of profit and loss ratios, balance sheet ratios, composite ratios
Functional classification: liquidity, solvency, activity (turnover) and profitability ratios
Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities; significance; ideal 2:1
Quick (liquid) ratio = quick assets / current liabilities; quick assets exclude inventories and prepaid expenses; ideal 1:1
Numericals: compute current and quick ratios; find current assets/liabilities from given ratio and working capital
Debt-equity ratio = long-term debts / shareholders' funds
Debt to capital employed ratio
Proprietary ratio = shareholders' funds / total assets
Total assets to debt ratio
Interest coverage ratio = net profit before interest and tax / interest on long-term debt
Computing capital employed, shareholders' funds and long-term debt from a balance sheet
Inventory turnover ratio = cost of revenue from operations / average inventory
Computing cost of revenue from operations and average inventory (with and without gross profit given)
Trade receivables turnover ratio = credit revenue from operations / average trade receivables (including bills receivable)
Trade payables turnover ratio = net credit purchases / average trade payables
Average collection and payment periods derived from turnover ratios
Net assets (capital employed) turnover ratio
Fixed assets turnover ratio
Working capital turnover ratio
Gross profit ratio = gross profit / net revenue from operations x 100
Operating ratio = (cost of revenue from operations + operating expenses) / revenue from operations x 100
Operating profit ratio = operating profit / revenue from operations x 100; relation with operating ratio
Net profit ratio on profit before tax and on profit after tax
Return on investment (return on capital employed) = PBIT / capital employed x 100
Numericals: compute profitability ratios from statement of profit and loss and balance sheet
Effect of given transactions on a ratio (increase, decrease, no change), e.g. on current or debt-equity ratio
Finding missing figures (inventory, current liabilities, revenue) from given ratios
Comprehensive question computing several ratios from given financial statements
Meaning of cash flow statement and its objective: sources and uses of cash and cash equivalents over a period
Assessing liquidity and ability to generate cash, short-term planning, comparisons, evaluating changes in net assets
Cash includes cash in hand and demand deposits
Cash equivalents: short-term highly liquid investments with maturity of three months or less; current investments treated as marketable securities
Bank overdraft and cash credit treated as short-term borrowings (financing activities)
Cash inflows and outflows; transactions that do not result in cash flow (movement within cash and cash equivalents)

sections.name: 10.5 Classification of Activities for the Preparation of Cash Flow Statement

concepts.text: Operating activities: principal revenue-producing activities with examples
Investing activities: purchase and sale of long-term assets and investments with examples
Financing activities: changes in owners' capital and borrowings with examples
Treatment of interest and dividend paid/received for financial vs non-financial enterprises
Treatment of income tax paid and its refund
Exercise type: classify given items into operating, investing or financing activities

sections.name: 10.6 Ascertaining the Net Cash Flow from Operating Activities

concepts.text: Indirect method (only method in CBSE syllabus): start from net profit before tax
Adding back non-cash and non-operating items: depreciation, amortisation of goodwill/patents, loss on sale of assets, interest paid
Deducting non-operating incomes: profit on sale of assets/investments, interest and dividends received
Operating profit before working capital changes
Adjusting changes in current assets and current liabilities (increase/decrease rules)
Deducting income tax paid to get net cash from operating activities
Adjustment for transfer to reserves, proposed dividend of previous year (AS 4) and interim dividend

sections.name: 10.7 Ascertaining the Net Cash Flow from Investing and Financing Activities

concepts.text: Investing: purchase/sale of fixed assets and investments using ledger accounts and additional information
Financing: issue/redemption of shares and debentures, long-term borrowings, interest and dividend paid
Preparing working accounts (machinery, provision for depreciation, provision for tax) to find hidden figures
Format of cash flow statement under AS 3 (Revised)
Reconciliation of net increase/decrease with opening and closing cash and cash equivalents
Numericals: prepare a complete cash flow statement from comparative balance sheets and additional information
Note: direct method is outside the CBSE syllabus
